examples.ko: 일요일 오후에 동네를 어슬렁어슬렁 걸어 다녔어요.
examples.en: On Sunday afternoon I strolled around the neighborhood.
The cat is prowling around the yard.

examples.ko: 수업이 끝났는데도 그는 어슬렁어슬렁 교실을 나갔어요.
examples.en: Even though class was over, he sauntered out of the classroom.

examples.ko: 급할 것 없다는 듯이 어슬렁어슬렁 걸어오네요.
examples.en: He's ambling over as if he's in no hurry at all.

examples.ko: 약속 시각이 한 시간이나 넘어서야 그는 어슬렁어슬렁 나타났어요.
examples.en: He only sauntered in after the meeting time was over by a whole hour.

examples.ko: 시장 안을 어슬렁어슬렁 구경하다 보면 시간이 금방 가요.
examples.en: If you wander around the market looking at things, time flies.

explain: '느릿느릿'이 속도만 말한다면 '어슬렁어슬렁'은 뚜렷한 목적 없이 여유롭게, 때로는 게으르게 걷는 모습까지 보여 줘요. '어슬렁거리다'처럼 동사로도 자주 말해요. 급한 일이 있는 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: While '느릿느릿' only describes slow speed, '어슬렁어슬렁' also shows walking around without a clear purpose, in a relaxed or sometimes lazy way. People also use the verb form '어슬렁거리다'. You would not use it for someone who has something urgent to do.

examples.en: The puppy is wandering around in front of the door.

examples.ko: 할 일 없이 집 앞에서 어슬렁어슬렁하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't hang around in front of the house with nothing to do.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 아까부터 가게 앞을 어슬렁어슬렁했어요.
examples.en: That person has been loitering in front of the shop since a while ago.

examples.ko: 방학이라 하루 종일 집 안에서 어슬렁어슬렁하고 있어요.
examples.en: It's vacation, so I'm just lazing around the house all day.

examples.ko: 수상한 사람이 골목에서 어슬렁어슬렁하는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a suspicious person lurking around in the alley.

examples.ko: 약속 시간 전에 역 근처를 어슬렁어슬렁해도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: It's fine to stroll around the station before our meeting time.

explain: '어슬렁어슬렁'에 '하다'가 붙은 동사로, 목적 없이 천천히 돌아다닐 때 써요. '어슬렁거리다', '어슬렁대다'처럼 말하기도 해요. 상황에 따라 한가로운 느낌도 되고, 수상하게 서성이는 느낌도 돼요.
explain_en: This verb comes from '어슬렁어슬렁' and is used when someone walks around slowly without a purpose. People also say '어슬렁거리다' or '어슬렁대다'. Depending on the situation it can feel relaxed or like someone loitering suspiciously.

examples.en: The dawn sky is faintly getting light.
The building looked dim through the fog.
I vaguely remember things from my childhood.
Moonlight comes faintly into the room.
That person's face comes back to me dimly.

examples.ko: 저녁 무렵 골목에 불빛이 어슴푸레 켜졌어요.
examples.en: Toward evening, lights came on dimly in the alley.

explain: '희미하게'와 비슷하지만 '어슴푸레'는 새벽이나 저녁처럼 어둑한 빛 속에서 흐릿하게 보이는 분위기가 강해요. 기억이 흐릿할 때도 쓸 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '어스름'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '희미하게' (faintly), but '어슴푸레' carries a stronger feeling of things looking blurry in dim light, like dawn or dusk. You can also use it for a hazy memory. A related word is '어스름'.

examples.en: After the sun sets, the street gets dim.

examples.ko: 새벽의 어슴푸레한 빛 속에서 산책을 시작했어요.
examples.en: I started my walk in the faint light of dawn.
My childhood memories are hazy now.
You haven't turned on the light, so the room is dim.

examples.ko: 어슴푸레하게 밝아 오는 아침 하늘이 예뻐요.
examples.en: The morning sky slowly brightening is beautiful.
I can see a faint island in the distance.

explain: '환하다'의 반대처럼 빛이 약해서 잘 안 보일 때 쓰고, 기억이 흐릿한 것에도 써요. '어렴풋하다'도 비슷하지만 '어슴푸레하다'는 어둑한 빛의 느낌이 더 잘 살아 있어요. 주로 '어슴푸레한 빛', '어슴푸레하게 보이다'로 써요.
explain_en: It works like the opposite of '환하다' (bright) when the light is weak and things are hard to see, and it can also describe a hazy memory. '어렴풋하다' is similar, but '어슴푸레하다' keeps more of the feeling of dim light. It is mostly used in phrases like '어슴푸레한 빛' and '어슴푸레하게 보이다'.

examples.en: The prices at the two shops are about the same.
Those singers' voices are so alike that I mix them up.

examples.ko: 어슷비슷한 디자인이 너무 많아서 고르기 어려워요.
examples.en: There are so many similar designs that it's hard to choose.
Their ages and heights are so alike that they look like brothers.
The candidates' pledges are all pretty much the same.
The two people's scores came out about even.

explain: '비슷하다'보다 큰 차이가 없이 다 거기서 거기라는 느낌이 강해요. 고르거나 비교할 때 '이것도 저것도 별 차이 없다'고 말하는 상황에 잘 어울려요. '고만고만하다'와도 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: Compared with '비슷하다', it strongly suggests that things are all about the same with no big difference. It fits situations where you choose or compare and say there is little difference between this and that. It is also used much like '고만고만하다'.

examples.en: Please cut the green onion on the diagonal.
For diagonal cutting, you tilt the knife and slice.
I cut the carrot on the diagonal and put it in the stir-fry.
Topping it with diagonally cut chili peppers looks nice.

examples.ko: 어슷썰기와 송송 썰기는 모양이 많이 달라요.
examples.en: Diagonal cutting and thin round slicing give very different shapes.
The cookbook says to cut on the diagonal.

explain: 파, 오이, 고추처럼 길쭉한 재료를 비스듬히 써는 방법으로, 레시피에서 자주 만나요. 동그랗게 써는 '송송 썰기', 가늘게 써는 '채썰기'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. '어슷하게 썰다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: This is a way of slicing long ingredients like green onions, cucumbers and chili peppers at an angle, and you will meet it in recipes. It helps to learn it together with '송송 썰기' (round slicing) and '채썰기' (julienne). People also say '어슷하게 썰다'.

examples.en: Whoa, you can't sit there!
Oops, your umbrella fell on the floor!

examples.ko: 어어, 잠깐만요, 저 아직 안 탔어요!
examples.en: Hey, wait a second, I haven't gotten on yet!

examples.ko: 어어, 이 컴퓨터가 왜 갑자기 꺼지지요?
examples.en: Hey, why is this computer suddenly turning off?
Whoa, it's dangerous if you go that way!
Oh no, the cup is about to tip over!

explain: 갑자기 놀라거나 뭔가 잘못되려고 할 때 급하게 내는 소리예요. 한 번 '어' 하는 것보다 두 번 반복하면 더 다급하고 당황한 느낌이 나요. 보통 뒤에 쉼표를 두고 하려는 말을 이어요.
explain_en: This is a quick sound you make when you are suddenly startled or something is about to go wrong. Repeating it twice sounds more urgent and flustered than a single '어'. It is usually followed by a comma and then what you want to say.

examples.en: The bride is truly lovely.

examples.ko: 어여쁜 아가씨가 꽃을 들고 서 있어요.
examples.en: A pretty young lady is standing there holding flowers.

examples.ko: 아이가 웃는 모습이 참 어여뻐 보여요.
examples.en: The child looks so lovely when smiling.
My grandmother calls me her lovely granddaughter.
When spring came, the flowers bloomed beautifully.

examples.ko: 어여쁜 한복을 입은 아이들이 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: The children in pretty hanbok lined up.

explain: '예쁘다'를 좀 더 정감 있고 예스럽게 말하는 느낌이에요. 노랫말이나 시, 어른이 아이를 귀여워하는 말에서 어울려요. 친구끼리 일상 대화에서는 보통 '예쁘다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It feels like a warmer, slightly old-fashioned way of saying '예쁘다'. It suits song lyrics, poems, and adults fondly talking about children. In everyday talk between friends, people usually just say '예쁘다'.

examples.en: I've become a proper university student now.
My younger sibling has settled in as a full-fledged working adult.
It was a small shop, but they put up a proper sign.
The child has become a proper young lady before I knew it.

examples.ko: 어엿한 회사원이 되고 나니 부모님이 기뻐하세요.
examples.en: Now that I'm a proper office worker, my parents are happy.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 이제 어엿한 맛집이 됐어요.
examples.en: That restaurant has become a proper famous eatery.

explain: 남 앞에 내놓아도 부끄럽지 않게 번듯하고 당당하다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '어엿한 대학생', '어엿한 어른'처럼 신분이나 자격을 나타내는 명사 앞에서 써요. 어리거나 작던 것이 자라서 인정받을 만해졌을 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It gives the feeling of being presentable and confident enough to show to others without embarrassment. It usually appears before a noun of status or qualification, like '어엿한 대학생' or '어엿한 어른'. It fits when something young or small has grown into something worthy of recognition.

en: being unspeakable; being staggering; being absurd

examples.ko: 지각한 사람이 오히려 나한테 화를 내서 어이가 없었어요.
examples.en: The person who was late got angry at me instead, and I was dumbfounded.

examples.ko: 열 번이나 설명했는데 또 같은 걸 묻다니 어이가 없네요.
examples.en: I explained it ten times and you're asking the same thing again? That's unbelievable.
It was so absurd that all I could do was laugh in disbelief.

examples.ko: 그 사람 변명을 들으니 어이가 없어서 말이 안 나와요.
examples.en: Hearing that person's excuse leaves me speechless.

examples.ko: 가격이 어이없을 만큼 비싸서 그냥 나왔어요.
examples.en: The price was so ridiculously high that I just walked out.

examples.ko: 어이없게도 제가 산 물건이 하루 만에 고장 났어요.
examples.en: Absurdly, the thing I bought broke down in a single day.

explain: 거의 '어이가 없다', '어이없다' 꼴로 써서, 기가 막히고 황당해서 말문이 막힐 때 말해요. '어처구니없다', '황당하다'와 비슷해요. '어이!'처럼 사람을 부르는 반말도 있지만 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the forms '어이가 없다' or '어이없다' when you are so astonished or baffled that you cannot find words. It is close to '어처구니없다' and '황당하다'. There is also a casual call '어이!' to get someone's attention, but it can sound rude.

examples.en: Whoa, I almost missed my step.
Oof, I didn't know it was this heavy.
Oops, I spilled the coffee!
Whoa, you startle me when you come out so suddenly!

examples.ko: 어이쿠, 정말 미안해요, 앞을 못 봤어요.
examples.en: Oops, I'm so sorry, I didn't see you.
Goodness, it's already this late.

explain: 깜짝 놀랐을 때, 실수했을 때, 몸이 아프거나 힘들 때 나오는 소리예요. 비슷한 소리로 '아이쿠', '어이구'가 있어요. 말투가 조금 정겹고 가벼워서 일상 대화에서 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: This is the sound people make when startled, when they make a mistake, or when something hurts or is tiring. Similar sounds are '아이쿠' and '어이구'. The tone is a little warm and light, so it fits everyday conversation.

examples.ko: 어정쩡한 태도로는 협상에서 원하는 것을 얻기 어려워요.
examples.en: With a wishy-washy attitude, it's hard to get what you want in a negotiation.

examples.ko: 점심을 먹기에는 이르고 간식을 먹기에는 늦은 어정쩡한 시간이에요.
examples.en: It's an in-between time, too early for lunch and too late for a snack.
The clothes are awkwardly big, so they're uncomfortable to wear.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이에서 어정쩡하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I stood awkwardly in between the two people.
I gave a vague answer and caused a misunderstanding.

examples.ko: 어정쩡한 자세로 오래 앉아 있었더니 허리가 아파요.
examples.en: I sat in an awkward position for a long time, and now my back hurts.

explain: 이쪽도 저쪽도 아닌 애매한 상태나 태도를 말할 때 써요. 보통 '어정쩡한', '어정쩡하게', '어정쩡해요'처럼 '-하다'가 붙은 꼴로 써요. 대답, 태도, 크기, 자세, 시간 등에 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a state or attitude that is neither one thing nor the other. It is normally used with '-하다' attached, as in '어정쩡한', '어정쩡하게' and '어정쩡해요'. It can describe answers, attitudes, sizes, postures and times.

en: all sorts of people; Tom, Dick and Harry; the rabble

examples.en: All sorts of random people gathered at that party.

examples.ko: 아무나 어중이떠중이를 다 뽑을 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't just hire any Tom, Dick or Harry.
That gathering is noisy because all kinds of people are there.

examples.ko: 어중이떠중이까지 다 나서니 일이 더 꼬였어요.
examples.en: With every Tom, Dick and Harry getting involved, things got even more tangled.
I'm not just some random person, I'm a real expert.

examples.ko: 어중이떠중이 말은 듣지 말고 직접 확인하세요.
examples.en: Don't listen to just anybody, check it yourself.

explain: 별 볼 일 없는 여러 사람을 한꺼번에 낮잡아 말할 때 써요. 사람을 낮추는 표현이라 상대방에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 돼요. 말하는 사람이 '내가 보기에 별로인 사람들'이라고 느낄 때 쓰는 말투예요.
explain_en: It is used to look down on a crowd of ordinary or unimpressive people all at once. Because it belittles people, it is rude to use it directly about the person you are talking to. It reflects the speaker's feeling of 'people who don't impress me'.

examples.ko: 어쭙잖은 위로는 오히려 더 상처가 돼요.
examples.en: Clumsy comfort can hurt even more.
I pretended to know something with half-baked knowledge and got embarrassed.
Don't try to teach with such laughable skills.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 어쭙잖은 농담에 아무도 웃지 않았어요.
examples.en: Nobody laughed at that person's lame joke.
I'm sorry if what I said sounded presumptuous.

examples.ko: 어쭙잖은 변명은 하지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to make feeble excuses.

explain: 제 분수에 맞지 않게 어설프고 우스꽝스러울 때 약간 비웃는 투로 써요. 주로 '어쭙잖은 + 명사', '어쭙잖게'로 쓰고, 자기 말을 낮출 때도 써요. '어줍잖다'는 틀린 표기이니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is used with a slightly mocking tone for something clumsy and laughable that is out of proportion to one's ability. It mostly appears as '어쭙잖은 + noun' or '어쭙잖게', and sometimes speakers use it to be modest about their own words. Be careful, because '어줍잖다' is a wrong spelling.

examples.en: I stood up suddenly and my head is spinning.

examples.ko: 높은 곳에서 아래를 보니 눈앞이 어찔했어요.
examples.en: When I looked down from a high place, everything swam before my eyes.
I felt dizzy, so I sat down for a moment.

examples.ko: 약 냄새를 맡자 어찔하면서 속이 울렁거렸어요.
examples.en: When I smelled the medicine, I felt dizzy and nauseous.
I walked across a dizzyingly high bridge.
I was so shocked that I felt faint for a moment.

explain: '어지럽다'가 계속 빙빙 도는 느낌이라면 '어찔하다'는 갑자기 순간적으로 핑 도는 느낌이에요. '아찔하다'와 비슷하게 쓰이는데 높은 곳이나 놀란 순간에 잘 어울려요. 보통 '머리가 어찔하다', '눈앞이 어찔하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: While '어지럽다' feels like a continuous spinning, '어찔하다' is a sudden, momentary swoon. It is used similarly to '아찔하다' and fits high places or startling moments. It is usually said as '머리가 어찔하다' or '눈앞이 어찔하다'.

examples.en: I lost in a ridiculous way, but I actually ended up laughing.

examples.ko: 어처구니없이 간단한 실수 때문에 일을 망쳤어요.
examples.en: I ruined the job because of an absurdly simple mistake.

examples.ko: 그는 어처구니없이 긴 줄을 보고 포기했어요.
examples.en: He saw the ridiculously long line and gave up.
I was shocked that it sold for an absurdly high price.
Can you believe I stupidly lost the documents?
The fight that started over something ridiculous lasted a long time.

explain: 기가 막히고 황당한 일을 말할 때 써요. '어이없이', '황당하게'와 비슷하고, 보통 좋지 않거나 믿기 어려운 일에 붙어요. 형용사 '어처구니없다'의 활용형이라 '어처구니없는 일'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: It is used for things that are so absurd they leave you stunned. It is close to '어이없이' and '황당하게', and usually attaches to bad or hard-to-believe events. It is the adverb form of the adjective '어처구니없다', which also appears as in '어처구니없는 일'.

examples.ko: 올해는 날씨 때문에 어획량이 크게 줄었어요.
examples.en: This year the catch dropped sharply because of the weather.

examples.ko: 이 바다는 오징어 어획량이 많기로 유명해요.
examples.en: This sea is famous for its large squid catch.

examples.ko: 어획량이 늘면 생선 값이 내려갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the catch increases, fish prices may go down.

examples.ko: 어촌 사람들은 어획량에 따라 수입이 달라져요.
examples.en: People in fishing villages see their income change depending on the catch.
The government decided to limit the catch.
The catch doubled compared with last year.

explain: 물고기를 잡은 양을 말하고, 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '어획량이 늘다/줄다', '어획량을 제한하다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 일상에서는 '잡은 양'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It means the amount of fish caught, and it often appears in news and economic talk. It pairs with verbs as in '어획량이 늘다/줄다' and '어획량을 제한하다'. In daily speech people may also say '잡은 양'.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 산에 억새가 하얗게 피어요.
examples.en: In autumn, silver grass blooms white on the mountains.
The silver grass swaying in the wind is beautiful.
Shall we go to the mountain this weekend to see the silver grass?

examples.ko: 억새 사이로 난 길을 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: I slowly walked along the path through the silver grass.
The silvery grass glittered in the sunset.
On Jeju Island there are many hills famous for silver grass.

explain: 가을 산과 들의 풍경을 말할 때 자주 나오는 식물이에요. 물가에서 자라는 '갈대'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 억새는 주로 산이나 들에서 볼 수 있어요. 보통 '억새가 피다', '억새가 흔들리다'처럼 가을 분위기와 함께 말해요.
explain_en: This plant often appears when people describe autumn scenery on mountains and fields. It is easy to confuse with '갈대' (reed), which grows near water, while '억새' is mainly seen on mountains and fields. It is usually used with an autumn mood, as in '억새가 피다' and '억새가 흔들리다'.

examples.ko: 산 정상에 넓은 억새밭이 펼쳐져 있어요.
examples.en: A wide field of silver grass stretches out at the mountain top.
Last weekend we took a family photo in the silver grass field.

examples.ko: 바람이 불자 억새밭이 은빛 물결처럼 일렁였어요.
examples.en: When the wind blew, the field rippled like silver waves.

examples.ko: 억새밭 사이로 좁은 길이 나 있어요.
examples.en: A narrow path runs through the silver grass field.
Every autumn, people flock to see the silver grass fields.
There is a small cafe near the silver grass field.

explain: 억새가 넓게 자란 곳을 말해요. 가을 나들이나 여행 이야기에서 '억새밭이 펼쳐지다', '억새밭을 걷다'처럼 자주 써요. 억새를 보러 가는 곳이 많아서 가을이면 안내문에도 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a place where silver grass grows over a wide area. In stories about autumn outings and trips, you often hear '억새밭이 펼쳐지다' and '억새밭을 걷다'. Many places are visited just to see silver grass, so the word often appears on notices in autumn.

examples.en: In an oppressive atmosphere, it's hard to speak freely.

examples.ko: 주인공이 억압적인 집안을 박차고 나가는 장면이 이 소설의 절정이에요.
examples.en: The scene where the main character storms out of the oppressive family is the climax of this novel.
The students are dissatisfied because of the oppressive rules.

examples.ko: 지나치게 억압적인 교육은 아이를 힘들게 해요.
examples.en: Overly repressive education makes children suffer.

examples.ko: 억압적인 정치에 맞서 사람들이 광장에 모였어요.
examples.en: People gathered in the square to stand against the oppressive politics.
I quit because of a boss who acted in a controlling way.

explain: 보통 '억압적인 분위기/가정/정책/체제'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 써요. 반대로 말할 때는 '자유로운', '개방적인'을 쓸 수 있어요. '억압적이다', '억압적으로'처럼도 활용돼요.
explain_en: It is usually placed before a noun, as in '억압적인 분위기', '억압적인 가정', '억압적인 정책' and '억압적인 체제'. For the opposite, you can use '자유로운' or '개방적인'. It also works in forms like '억압적이다' and '억압적으로'.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 억지웃음을 짓느라 얼굴이 아팠어요.
examples.en: My face hurt from faking smiles all day.
I was sad, but I forced a smile in front of my friend.

examples.ko: 그의 억지웃음이 어색해서 오히려 마음이 쓰였어요.
examples.en: His forced smile looked awkward, which actually made me worry.
The joke wasn't funny, but I got through it with a forced smile.
I could feel the true feelings hiding behind the forced smile.

examples.ko: 사진 찍을 때 억지웃음이 나와서 어색해요.
examples.en: When I take photos a fake smile comes out and it looks awkward.

explain: '억지웃음을 짓다'처럼 마음에 없는데 일부러 웃을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요. '억지로 웃다'라고 풀어 말해도 돼요. '쓴웃음'은 씁쓸한 마음에서 나오는 웃음이고, '억지웃음'은 분위기를 맞추려고 일부러 웃는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It pairs naturally with '짓다', as in '억지웃음을 짓다', when you smile on purpose without really feeling it. You can also say it more plainly as '억지로 웃다'. '쓴웃음' comes from bitter feelings, while '억지웃음' mostly feels like smiling on purpose to fit the mood.

examples.en: My mother worked tirelessly and raised us.

examples.ko: 그는 억척같이 돈을 모아 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: He saved money relentlessly and opened a shop.

examples.ko: 억척같이 버티다 보니 좋은 날이 왔어요.
examples.en: I held on stubbornly, and good days came.
Thanks to studying with grit, I passed the exam.
That lady runs her business at the market with great determination.
Even though it was hard, I endured with grit.

explain: 어려운 상황에서도 모질고 끈질기게 해 나가는 모습을 말해요. 생활력 강한 모습을 말할 때 많이 쓰고, 존경과 안쓰러움이 함께 느껴지기도 해요. 비슷한 '악착같이'는 더 독하게 달라붙는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes pushing on doggedly and tenaciously even in hard circumstances. It is often used for people with strong survival skills, and it can carry both respect and a touch of pity. The similar '악착같이' feels more like clinging on fiercely.

examples.en: That lady at the market is really tough and determined.

examples.ko: 억척스러운 어머니 덕분에 우리는 잘 자랐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to our tenacious mother, we grew up well.
He worked relentlessly and grew the shop.
I don't mind being called tenacious.
Sometimes that tenacious side of her makes me feel sorry for her.
Unlike how she looks, my younger sister studies with real grit.

explain: ㅂ 불규칙이라 '억척스러워요', '억척스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 어려움 속에서도 끈질기게 버티는 사람에게 쓰는데, 칭찬일 수도 있고 다소 거칠다고 보는 말일 수도 있어서 상대에게 직접 말할 때는 조심해요. '억척같이'와 같은 계열의 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular word, so it changes to '억척스러워요' and '억척스러운'. It is used for people who hold on tenaciously through hardship, and it can be praise or a slightly rough description, so be careful when saying it directly to someone. It belongs to the same family as '억척같이'.

en: not daring to do something; being unthinkable

examples.en: Buying an expensive car is out of the question for me.
With such a small salary, overseas travel was beyond my dreams.

examples.ko: 언감생심, 제가 어떻게 그런 자리를 바라겠어요.
examples.en: How could I even dare hope for such a position?

examples.ko: 집 한 채 갖는 건 언감생심 꿈도 못 꿔요.
examples.en: Owning a house is something I wouldn't even dare to dream of.
In this situation, studying abroad is out of the question.

examples.ko: 그 큰 상을 받으리라고는 언감생심 생각도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I wouldn't have dared even to imagine winning that big prize.

explain: 형편이나 처지 때문에 감히 바랄 수도 없는 일을 말할 때 써요. '…은 언감생심이다'로도 쓰고, 문장 앞에서 '언감생심 꿈도 못 꾸다'처럼 부사처럼도 써요. 조금 예스럽고 겸손하거나 자조하는 말투예요.
explain_en: It is used for something you cannot even dare to hope for because of your circumstances. It works as '…은 언감생심이다', and also at the front of a sentence like an adverb, as in '언감생심 꿈도 못 꾸다'. It sounds a little old-fashioned, modest or self-deprecating.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 언덕배기에 있어서 겨울에 오르기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Our house is on a hillside, so it's hard to climb in winter.
The night view from the top of the hill is wonderful.

examples.ko: 언덕배기를 따라 작은 집들이 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Small houses are clustered along the hill slope.
The children are flying kites on the hill.
I rode my bike up the steep hill.

examples.ko: 언덕배기 끝에 오래된 나무 한 그루가 서 있어요.
examples.en: At the end of the hill stands one old tree.

explain: '언덕'보다 입말 느낌이 강하고, 언덕의 꼭대기나 비탈진 곳을 정겹게 말할 때 어울려요. 동네 풍경을 이야기할 때 '언덕배기에 있는 집'처럼 많이 써요. 글에서는 '언덕'이 더 무난해요.
explain_en: It feels more colloquial than '언덕' and fits when you fondly refer to the top or slope of a hill. It is often used in descriptions of a neighborhood, as in '언덕배기에 있는 집'. In writing, '언덕' is the safer choice.

examples.ko: 그는 언변이 좋아서 사람들을 쉽게 설득해요.
examples.en: He is a good talker, so he persuades people easily.
A person with great speaking skills has an advantage in interviews.

examples.ko: 저는 언변이 없어서 발표가 늘 힘들어요.
examples.en: I'm not good with words, so presentations are always hard.
In sales, sincerity matters more than flashy talk.
That person captivated the audience with natural eloquence.
Speaking skills can improve with practice.

explain: '말솜씨'와 비슷하지만 좀 더 격식 있고 글 같은 느낌이에요. '언변이 좋다/뛰어나다/없다'처럼 짝지어 써요. '화려한 언변'은 말만 번지르르하다는 약간 부정적인 느낌도 줄 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '말솜씨' but feels a bit more formal and bookish. It pairs as in '언변이 좋다', '언변이 뛰어나다' and '언변이 없다'. '화려한 언변' can also carry a slightly negative sense of being all smooth talk.

examples.en: Teenagers' language habits are changing a lot.

examples.ko: 바른 언어생활을 위해 줄임말을 줄이기로 했어요.
examples.en: For proper language use, I decided to cut down on abbreviations.

examples.ko: 인터넷 때문에 우리의 언어생활이 크게 변했어요.
examples.en: The internet has greatly changed how we use language.

examples.ko: 가족과 함께 존댓말을 쓰며 건강한 언어생활을 해요.
examples.en: We use honorific speech in our family and keep healthy language habits.

examples.ko: 외국에서 살 때는 언어생활이 많이 불편했어요.
examples.en: When I lived abroad, communicating in the language was very inconvenient.
Please teach correct language habits at school.

explain: 일상에서 말과 글을 어떻게 쓰고 사는지를 크게 묶어 말할 때 써요. '바른 언어생활', '언어생활이 변하다'처럼 뉴스, 교육, 국어 수업에서 자주 보여요. 실제로 대화할 때는 '말하는 습관'이라고도 풀어서 말해요.
explain_en: It is used to talk in broad terms about how people use spoken and written language in daily life. You see it in news, education and Korean-language classes, as in '바른 언어생활' and '언어생활이 변하다'. In real conversation, people may also put it more plainly as '말하는 습관'.

examples.en: His compliment had a sting hidden in it, so I felt uneasy.
He said it with a smile, but there was a barb in it.

examples.ko: 언중유골이니 그 말의 속뜻을 잘 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: There's a hidden edge to it, so think carefully about what was really meant.

examples.ko: 부장님이 수고했다고 하셨는데 왠지 언중유골 같았어요.
examples.en: The manager said I did a good job, but somehow it felt loaded.
Everyone went quiet at the joke with a barb in it.

examples.ko: 그 말 속에 언중유골이 숨어 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems like there's a hidden jab inside that remark.

explain: 겉으로는 평범해 보이는 말 속에 비꼬거나 경고하는 속뜻이 있을 때 써요. 보통 '언중유골이다', '언중유골 같다'로 말해요. 같은 뜻의 순우리말 표현으로 '말 속에 뼈가 있다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when a remark that looks ordinary on the surface contains a sarcastic or warning meaning inside. It is usually said as '언중유골이다' or '언중유골 같다'. A native-Korean expression with the same sense is '말 속에 뼈가 있다'.
